pending_autograd_counterexample.interpretation: A caller must ensure a between-step boundary with no retained graph. Literal public-state restore is not autograd graph/version restore.

remaining_boundaries: The adapter cannot detect all external pending autograd graphs. The caller must establish a between-step boundary with no concurrent writer. An independent 2-element square-loss counterexample proves restored public bytes can coexist with a stale graph that raises on backward.
Successful copy_ increments PyTorch version counters. Unexpected-apply rollback does not rewind them. This is not a full autograd/object-graph transaction.

The demonstrated replay is one tiny synthetic Torch transition on the recorded runtime. No scientific learning kernel, scientific model/assets, field-control evaluation, bank, endpoint, fit, holdout or preregistration was imported, read or executed.

Caller-supplied context/architecture and separately held environment identity must be complete and trusted. Omitted external files, arbitrary Python program state and undeclared entropy sources cannot be discovered by this adapter.

Supported state is deliberately narrow: ordinary independent contiguous CPU tensors, fixed modes/configuration and stock non-differentiable non-fused SGD. No general device, tied-storage, arbitrary optimizer or scheduler support is qualified.

The adapter does not durably preserve failures or enforce a scientific work/resource ledger; a future runner must do so. No process-death, rollback allocation-failure or concurrent-mutation guarantee is established.
A 56,988-byte toy checkpoint under 64 KiB is not a real candidate state/output/trace bound. The foundation nine-class budget remains incomplete and its 2 GiB f_bavail gate remains unmet.
Original V5 scientific FAIL/no-admission and exact historical regression requirements remain unchanged. This receipt grants no admission, scientific execution or raw-upload authorization.
